articles.title: Osmania University receives USD 110,000 donation for engineering dept. from ex-student - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Osmania University received a USD 110,000 donation from alumnus Tella Gopal Rao through the Tella Sakamoto Foundation, USA. The funds will support facilities for digital mining technologies, research, and safety initiatives in both the Mining Engineering and Electrical Engineering departments.  The allocation also includes funding for construction work in the Electrical Engineering department.

articles.title: JoSAA Counselling 2026: IIT Kanpur sets up helpdesk to guide JEE Advanced qualifiers | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Kanpur has launched an official JoSAA Counselling helpdesk to assist JEE Advanced-qualified candidates during the ongoing counselling process. The initiative, introduced by the Academics and Career Council (AnC), provides access to verified student mentors through a WhatsApp community for personalized guidance on academic choices, campus life, and placement opportunities.  The institute will also host an online JoSAA Open House on June 9, 2026, featuring representatives from various departments to answer questions and provide information about the admission process. The registration and choice-filling process for JoSAA 2026 remains open until June 11.

articles.title: Rajasthan PTET 2026 Admit Card: VMOU PTET Admit Card 2026 Date, Time, Download Direct Link at ptetvmoukota2026.in
articles.rephrased_article: Vardhman Mahaveer Open University (VMOU) is expected to release the admit cards for the Rajasthan PTET exam today. Candidates who have applied can download their hall tickets from vmou.ac.in, checking details such as name, application number, roll number, date and time, exam centre, photograph, signature, and instructions.  Candidates are advised to carefully review the information on the admit card before downloading it for future reference.

articles.title: Delhi government ITI admission 2026: Registration opens today at itidelhi.admissions.nic.in
articles.rephrased_article: The Directorate of Training and Technical Education (DTTE), Government of NCT of Delhi, has opened the registration process for admission to Delhi Government Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) for the academic session 2026-27.  Candidates must complete their registration by visiting the official portal, itidelhi.admissions.nic.in and following the steps outlined in the instructions provided. The admission process includes registration, eligibility verification, merit preparation, and counselling rounds. Admission will be based on a merit-cum-counselling process.

articles.title: Let’s resist easy indictments of Indian Knowledge Systems | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Yogendra Yadav, a prominent Indian public intellectual, criticizes the current state of Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS), arguing that it is overly text-based and dismissive of oral traditions. He believes IKS should be more inclusive and connected to modern science, but his views are criticized by those who argue that Sanskrit plays a crucial role in connecting diverse Indian knowledge traditions.  The JANA Group, co-founded by Yadav, supports an open-source IKS initiative focused on the oral and folk traditions, while acknowledging the historical exclusions of Sanskrit and Brahmanical learning.

articles.title: University of Strathclyde offers £7,000 scholarship for international physics students | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The University of Strathclyde in Glasgow has announced a new scholarship worth £7,000 per year for international students entering a physics degree program starting in September 2026. The award is automatically granted to eligible new fee-paying international students who are entering either Year 1 or Year 2 of the full-time undergraduate program and will be applied directly towards tuition fees each academic year. Students must meet specific criteria, including being self-funded and not already receiving a scholarship from another source, and must complete enrollment by July 31, 2026.

articles.title: NCST invites applications for internships with Rs 15,000 stipend, last date June 18 | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) has launched online registration for its internship program. Eligible candidates can apply through the NCSTGRAMS portal at ncstgrams.gov.in, with applications closing on June 18th at 5 pm. The program selects around 10 students per intake and offers a stipend of Rs 15,000 upon completion of the one-month internship. Candidates must have a minimum of 60% in their qualifying examination and be either in their second year of graduation or have completed graduation.

articles.title: The 3 Crucial Windows: Why the First and Last 10 Minutes of a Child's Day Matter Most
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Swati Popat Vats, President of the Early Childhood Association, advocates for a "10-minute rule" to promote emotional strength in children.  She emphasizes that spending dedicated, distraction-free time with children – 10 minutes upon waking, bedtime, and during their day – fosters emotional security and resilience. Pavitra Shankar, an expert on child development, agrees, stating that love is not measured by time but by emotional availability. She highlights the importance of consistent engagement for building secure attachment and developing emotional regulation skills in children.  Dr. Shankar also emphasizes the significance of eye contact as a vital form of communication for children's brain development.

articles.title: Over 300 Osmania Law students turn ‘fail’ to ‘pass’ after revaluation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Osmania University has reversed the results of over 300 law students who were initially marked failed in their third-semester LLB examinations. The revised results show a significant improvement across multiple subjects, with more than 800 papers seeing grade increases. This includes eight papers jumping five grades from F to A, 141 moving from F to B, 158 from F to C, and 93 from F to D.

articles.title: SFI and DYFI protest NTA failures, demand Union Education Minister’s resignation - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students' Federation of India (SFI) and Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) jointly organized a protest in Vijayawada demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The protesters accused him of negligence for the failures of the National Testing Agency (NTA), including the NEET paper leak, irregularities in UGC-NET applications, flaws in CBSE evaluations, and the cancellation of CUET-UG examinations. They claimed the government has been handling the future of millions of students with disregard.

articles.title: Sharnbasveshwar PU College students excel in KCET - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharnbasveshwar Residential Composite PU College in Kalaburagi, Karnataka, saw several students achieve top ranks in the KCET 2026.  Channabasava K. secured the 27th rank in B.Pharm and other notable achievers include Simran Banu (35th rank in BNYS), Arnav Nagalikar (121st rank in BNYS), Harshvardhan Reddy (310th rank in Engineering), and Venkatesh Kulkarni (310th rank in Engineering). The college celebrated this academic success, attributing it to the collective efforts of students, faculty, and management.

articles.title: Rajan Gurukkal, Rajan Varughese step down as KSHEC vice-chairperson, member secretary - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajan Gurukkal and Rajan Varughese, the vice-chairperson and member secretary of the Kerala State Higher Education Council (KSHEC), have resigned from their positions. The duo led the council since 2017 and played a key role in implementing several reforms including the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUGP), the establishment of the SAAC, and the KIRF.  The KSHEC also facilitated digital transformation initiatives and launched programs like the Kairali Research Awards and Chief Minister’s Nava Kerala Postdoctoral Fellowships.

articles.title: Bicycles distributed to help rural girl students commuting to schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sri Satya Sai Seva Organisation distributed bicycles to girl students in Koyyapeta village, Visakhapatnam district, to ease their commute to schools and colleges. The initiative was prompted by Gurunatha Rao, a Bal Vikas Guru and Convener of the Reddypalli Bhajan Mandali, who brought the issue to the organization's attention.  The organisation aims to support education and reduce the daily travel burden on rural students.

articles.title: NEET UG 2026 re-exam city intimation slip released at neet.nta.nic.in; exam on June 21 | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has released the city intimation slip for the NEET UG 2026 re-examination, allowing candidates to check their allotted examination centers. The re-test, scheduled for June 21st after the May 3rd exam was cancelled due to paper leak allegations, will be held in pen and paper mode from 2 pm to 5:15 pm across 551 cities in India and 14 cities abroad. Candidates can download the slip by logging in with their application credentials, but it is not an admit card and should be used for travel and accommodation arrangements.

articles.title: ‘IIT gives you a bigger stage to grow’ | Life in an IIT | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mridusmita Deka, a 21-year-old student at IIT Guwahati, pursued Mechanical Engineering after initially considering Aerospace Engineering. She excelled in academics and extracurricular activities, including squash, astronomy, and cultural events, while also managing her time effectively and developing leadership skills. Deka credits her experiences at IIT Guwahati for transforming her into a more responsible and social individual.  She is currently exploring career paths within AI and ML, driven by her passion for problem-solving and continuous learning.

articles.title: Tavleen Singh writes: The problem in India is not unemployment but unemployability | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Tavleen Singh argues that the real problem in India is not unemployment but unemployability. She criticizes the current education system, citing its lack of focus on critical thinking and investment in infrastructure, as well as a history of neglect by political leaders. Singh suggests reforms like abolishing the University Grants Commission, encouraging student participation, and improving teacher training, along with increased investment in school infrastructure.  She calls for greater urgency to address these issues before India's children are disadvantaged in a globalized world.

articles.title: Five Government Tool Room and Training Centre students selected by Germany’s Rheinbahn AG - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Government Tool Room and Training Centre
articles.rephrased_article: Sharan Prakash Patil, Minister for Skill Development and Medical Education, presented Letters of Intent (LoIs) to five students from the Government Tool Room and Training Centre (GTTC) in Karnataka. These students were selected by Rheinbahn AG, a leading public transport operator in Germany, for placement under its German Ausbildung (dual vocational training) program beginning September 2026. The selection was announced at a felicitation ceremony held at Vikasa Soudha.

articles.title: State board students dominate CET toppers list - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Karnataka's Common Entrance Test (CET) results for 2026 show a shift in top rankings, with students from state board Pre-University colleges leading the way.  The engineering stream saw a majority of the top 10 positions occupied by students from State board-affiliated colleges, followed closely by other streams like B.V.Sc., B.Sc. (Agriculture), and Nursing. The results highlight a change in dominance for state board institutions over CBSE schools.

articles.title: CET: Poor performance by rural, government college and Kannada-medium students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Government PU colleges saw a poor performance in the CET-2026, with only 12 students ranking within the top 1,000. Rural students and those from Kannada-medium schools also performed poorly, with significantly fewer students achieving high rankings.  A total of 7,620 students from government colleges appeared for the exam, but none made it into the top 100 ranks.

articles.title: Vedant Shrivastava, Nisarga Adhikary and Sarthak Sidhant | The Gen Z trio that took on the CBSE - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Vedant Shrivastava, Nisarga Adhikary, and Sarthak Sidhant, three teenagers, became vocal critics of the Central Board of Secondary Education’s (CBSE) On-Screen Marking system after experiencing issues with its accuracy. Following public outcry and an admission by the board of flaws in the system, their concerns were validated.

articles.title: AISF demands white paper on DSC-2025 teacher recruitment process - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Sai Kumar, vice-president of the All India Students’ Federation (AISF), called for a white paper from the government regarding allegations of irregularities in the DSC-2025 teacher recruitment process.  He demanded an explanation from Education Minister Nara Lokesh and officials, following complaints from DSC candidates about unfair treatment, lack of transparency, and biased selection processes.

articles.title: UPSC Prelims 2026: What Ethics Questions Reveal About UPSC
articles.rephrased_article: The UPSC included ethics-oriented questions in the Prelims 2026 examination, surprising many aspirants. These questions tested candidates' ability to evaluate competing considerations, understand human behavior, and reflect on the consequences of different courses of action, encompassing all three dimensions of ethical decision-making: ethical, behavioral, and reflective. The exam appears to be assessing an applicant's capacity for ethical reasoning in a governance context, requiring them to navigate complex situations involving conflicting values and public interest. This shift towards incorporating ethical considerations into the selection process is significant, particularly in a welfare state like India, where ethical frameworks are crucial for effective governance.

articles.title: IIT Madras Team Takes India's Solar Car Dream To South Africa
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Madras students, part of the team Agnirath, are preparing to compete in the prestigious Sasol Solar Challenge in South Africa.  The eight-day race tests teams' engineering intelligence and energy management skills, with winners determined by the distance covered rather than speed. The team has redesigned their solar-powered vehicle to achieve an "energy-neutral" state, allowing it to run for extended periods at a constant 65 kilometers per hour. This competition offers a platform for showcasing Indian engineering on a global stage and demonstrating the potential of solar technology in shaping future mobility.

articles.title: A ‘thank-you’, and a word of caution from activist Sonam Wangchuk at the Cockroach Janta Party protest | The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Sonam Wangchuk, a popular education reform activist, praised the Indian government for allowing the protest against examination irregularities at Jantar Mantar.  He called it a "major achievement" and a "victory for India and even for the government," emphasizing that the movement was peaceful and aimed to achieve systemic reforms in education. Wangchuk urged the crowd to focus on broader goals, including equality in classrooms and access to quality education for all children, regardless of their background or location. He called for wider participation from citizens and ministers, believing that real change would come when policymakers themselves studied in government schools alongside everyone else.

articles.title: At private university event, Maharashtra minister Chandrakant Patil blasts public universities | Pune News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Soham Shah, a correspondent for The Indian Express, based in Pune, has transitioned his reporting from education to investigative and human rights stories. His recent work includes investigations into the Pune Municipal Corporation's policy changes on birth certificates and real estate irregularities involving political families.  He also published articles about faculty vacancies at Savitribai Phule Pune University, Maharashtra's controversial third language policy, and discrepancies in state education data despite rising student numbers. Shah is known for his focus on civil liberties and has championed the rights of marginalized groups through his reporting.
articles.civic_flag_reason: The article suggests abuse of power by a minister against public universities.

articles.title: CJP warns of nationwide agitation if Education Minister Pradhan not removed in seven days - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online campaign, organized a protest in New Delhi demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The CJP, which garnered over 22 million followers on Instagram, claims to represent the concerns of young people regarding irregularities in examinations and recruitment tests.  The group gave the government a seven-day deadline to address their demands or face nationwide protests. They emphasized that this is just the beginning of a broader youth movement focused on education and governance issues.

articles.title: SC ruling on creamy layer prompts demand for JEE category revision - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of OBC students in Kerala risk losing their reservation benefits in JEE Main and Advanced after the Supreme Court ruled that parental income from salary or agriculture cannot be the sole basis for creamy layer status. The ruling, which came in March 2023, has prompted demands for a revision of category declarations and JEE ranks prepared by the National Testing Agency (NTA).  Students and parents argue that many who were denied NCL certificates are now eligible for OBC reservation, prompting calls for the NTA to reconsider their category status.

articles.title: SC ruling on creamy layer prompts demand for JEE category revision - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Hundreds of OBC students in Kerala risk losing their reservation benefits in JEE Main and Advanced due to a recent Supreme Court ruling that redefined the criteria for creamy layer status. The court ruled that parental income from salary and agriculture cannot be solely used to determine creamy layer exclusion, prompting demands for revisions of category declarations and rankings by NTA. Students and parents argue that this ruling makes many previously denied NCL certificates eligible for OBC reservation.

articles.title: ‘Wants electrical engineering over CSE ‘: KCET 2026 topper Srajan BS spills his success secrets
articles.rephrased_article: Srajan B S, a 18-year-old student from Karnataka, secured the second rank in the KCET engineering entrance exam. He achieved this despite not studying for long hours and choosing to focus on consistent study habits rather than marathon sessions. Srajan's preparation involved self-study, weekly tests at his school, and a strong interest in electrical engineering which he pursued after being introduced to it by his mother during the pandemic.  He plans to pursue an undergraduate degree in Mechanical or Electrical Engineering from IITs or NITs and is considering further studies like Research and MTech.

articles.title: CET 2026 results announced in Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) released the results for the CET 2026 on June 6th, with over 2.9 million candidates eligible for admission to various professional courses.  Tanisha Karthik topped the engineering stream, while Nayana Gopi achieved first rank in Veterinary, Yoga and Naturopathy, B.Pharm, Pharma D, and Nursing. The counselling process will begin on June 10th, with mock results announced in four days.

articles.title: KCET Results 2026: Websites to check
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Exam Authority (KEA) will activate the KCET results link at 2 pm today, allowing candidates to check their scores on cetonline.karnataka.gov.in and karresults.nic.in.  A total of 3.1 to 3.2 lakh candidates appeared for the exam, with Tanisha Karthik topping the engineering exam. The results are provisional and candidates must download their marksheets from DigiLocker to enable mark retrieval for merit determination. After the results are released, students will participate in online counselling to choose their preferred colleges.

articles.title: KEA KCET Results 2026: How to check & download scorecards from cetonline.karnataka.gov.in, karresults.nic.in | Education News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) will announce the results of the Karnataka Common Entrance Test (KCET) today.  Eligible candidates can access their results by visiting the official websites at cetonline.karnataka.gov.in and karresults.nic.in. A total of 330,479 students registered for the exam, with approximately 310,000 to 320,000 participating. The KCET was held in two shifts on April 23 and 24, 2026, and the final answer key was released on May 10.

articles.title: After initial denial, CBSE invited ethical hacker to plug gaps in IT system - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) invited ethical hacker Nisarga Adhikary, 19, to help address security vulnerabilities in its IT ecosystem.  A team of cybersecurity experts from the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) worked for two weeks at the CBSE headquarters, patching critical vulnerabilities found in the OSM portal and the re-evaluation portal. The IIT teams identified seven to eight critical vulnerabilities, including an authentication bypass and unauthorized administrative access, in the portals developed by COEMPT Eduteck.  The team also discovered that the external vendor had severely misconfigured cloud storage buckets, keeping unsecured backups of student answer scripts on their servers.  To address these issues, the IIT experts set up a "Red Team versus Blue Team" dynamic to test and defend the portals. The CBSE has issued an advisory to departments to consider cybersecurity hygiene when hiring tech vendors.

articles.title: Relief for JEE qualifiers hit by CBSE OSM Row: IIT Roorkee allows seat allocation even below 75%
articles.rephrased_article: IIT Roorkee announced that students who fall short of the mandatory Class 12 percentage requirement for JEE Advanced 2026 will still be allowed to participate in JoSAA counselling and receive seat allotments, provided they submit a revised scorecard meeting the eligibility threshold by July 15, 2026.  The decision comes in response to concerns raised about errors in CBSE’s On-Screen Marking system for Class 12 evaluations, which have left some students ineligible for IIT admission despite clearing JEE Advanced. Students must submit their revised scorecards to orgjee@iitr.ac.in once they are available.

articles.title: ‘Social media protects people from being held accountable’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Hindu hosted its flagship youth engagement platform, 'The Hindu Huddle on Campus', at Amity University. The event focused on the impact of social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok on student mental health. Vishu Dev C.H., a faculty member from Amity School for Communication Enhancement and Transformation, moderated a panel discussion that included students Aaditi Singh, Stuti Ranjan, Shafin Shabeer, and Anishka Chandra.  The Hindu's Deputy Chief of Bureau, B.S. Satish Kumar, emphasized the need for proper supervision and digital literacy to mitigate potential negative effects.

articles.title: Pulluvila anganwadi in Thiruvananthapuram gets own building - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Positive Power for Children, a German non-profit organization led by Maria Kasselmann, and Heart for Kingdom have collaborated to build a permanent anganwadi building in Pulluvila ward of the Karumkulam grama panchayat. The new facility, inaugurated on Friday, will provide improved early childhood care and education services due to its spacious classroom, kitchen, storage room, toilet facilities, and child-friendly play equipment. Josephine, an anganwadi teacher, credits the project's success to the ward member's coordination efforts and overcoming administrative hurdles.

articles.title: New principal for 170 year-old-school in Belagavi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Reverend Father Eric Mathias assumed the role of Principal at St. Paul’s High School in Belagavi, Karnataka, on June 4th.  A Jesuit priest with extensive experience in education and social work, Mathias has served as principal for several institutions across Karnataka. He was welcomed by outgoing Principal Rev. Fr. Simon Fernandes, who will now lead at St. Loyola High School in Goa. Mathias also met with local authorities and community leaders.

articles.title: Safeguards sought against misuse of menstrual leave in schools - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: K. Prathibha, a medical officer from Tanur, has written to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan urging the government to implement strict guidelines and mandatory medical certification for schoolgirls seeking menstrual leave.  Dr. Prathibha suggests that students experiencing severe physical or psychological difficulties during menstruation should be granted leave based on an annual certificate issued by a government female doctor, and that requests be handled by a female teacher.

articles.title: Move to convert one of the oldest boys’ schools kicks up a row - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: St. Joseph’s Boys’ Higher Secondary School
articles.rephrased_article: The Education department has approved the admission of girl students to St. Joseph’s Boys’ Higher Secondary School in Kozhikode city, a move that has sparked controversy.  While school management and staff claim the decision was made based on parental and student demands, former students from the 233-year-old institution argue that it will diminish the school's historical status as one of the oldest boys’ schools in the state. They also express concerns about the lack of gender sensitisation programs and the adequacy of existing infrastructure to support the transition.

articles.title: Free bus pass for all students: Educationists and student organisations welcome move - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State government has extended its free bus pass scheme to all students of schools and colleges in Karnataka.  Niranjanaradhya V.P., a developmental educationist, praised the decision, stating it will benefit poor and underprivileged students. Student organizations like AIDSO and ABVP also welcomed the move, urging for smooth implementation from the start of the academic year.

articles.title: UPSC Essentials subject-wise quiz : Economy (Week 165)
articles.rephrased_article: UPSC Essentials brings subject-wise quizzes to help with UPSC exam preparation.  The article discusses the importance of millets, the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) scheme, flex-fuel vehicles, and the Real Effective Exchange Rate (REER). The author explains that these topics are frequently tested in the UPSC Prelims exam.

articles.title: Alpha School’s Ritzy New York City Campus Costs $65,000 a Year—but Isn’t Actually a School | WIRED
articles.rephrased_article: Alpha School, a company aiming to redefine education through AI, hosted information sessions in Lower Manhattan for wealthy New York City parents. The sessions were led by MacKenzie Price, co-founder of the company, and its billionaire principal, Joe Liemandt.  The sessions aimed to persuade families to enroll their children at Alpha's new campus, which is a homeschooling center disguised as a private school. The campus costs $65,000 per year.

articles.title: TS LAWCET, PGLCET Results 2026: Scorecards releasing today at 4 pm at lawcet.tgche.ac.in
articles.rephrased_article: The Osmania University, Hyderabad, will release the TS LAWCET and PGLCET 2026 results today (June 4) at 4 pm. Candidates can access their scorecards online at lawcet.tgche.ac.in and download rank cards from the official candidate portal.  The results document includes the candidate's name, roll number, total marks, rank, and qualifying status. Students are advised to thoroughly check all information on their scorecards and report any discrepancies to authorities without delay.

articles.title: Nigeria’s second-chance schools: women balancing study and survival | Features News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Women in northern Nigeria are returning to school after years away, but face challenges balancing childcare and economic responsibilities. The Women Centre for Continuing Education (WCCE) in Sokoto State provides a three-year curriculum for primary education, helping women like Habiba Abubakar pursue their dreams of becoming nurses or teachers.  However, students often juggle academic activities with household duties, relying on family support networks to remain in school. Despite these challenges, the WCCE has trained many skilled professionals and offers free tuition, but some students still struggle with transportation costs and other expenses. UNICEF reports that over half of girls in the region are not attending school due to poverty, early marriage, and restrictive gender norms.  To address this issue, organizations like Basileia Vulnerable Persons Rights Initiative (BVPRI) advocate for a lifelong learning framework that recognizes education as a continuous right and opportunity.

articles.title: PSEB class 10, 12 supplementary exam 2026: Registration process starts, check important dates
articles.rephrased_article: The Punjab Board of School Education (PSEB) has opened registration for the Class 10 and 12 supplementary exams for 2026. Students can apply online at pseb.ac.in to appear in compartment, improvement, re-appear, additional subject, or Punjab Open School examinations. The deadline for submitting applications is June 15, 2026, with a late fee option until June 22nd.  The supplementary exams are for students who did not pass one or more subjects in the main examination and those seeking to improve marks or take an additional subject.

articles.title: 3 coaching centres sealed days before recruitment exam, student anxiety simmers in Prayagraj | Lucknow News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Priya Rajput and Pankaj Singh, aspiring police constables, are facing disruption to their studies after the Prayagraj Development Authority sealed three prominent coaching centers. The action was taken on May 31st, citing violations of mandatory formalities.  The owners of the institutes, including Maroof Ahmed from Super Climax Coaching and Ravi P Tiwari from Target On Coaching, claim that they are being penalized for participating in a candlelight march protesting alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations. The protesters demanded transparency and accountability from the government, while police have booked two prominent figures in the stir on charges of breach of peace.  The UPSSSC has stated that the examination was conducted with integrity and no evidence of malpractice was found.

articles.title: Thousands of teachers likely to lose jobs in Calicut varsity’s self-financing colleges - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: University of Calicut is planning to make the UGC-NET or a PhD mandatory for faculty appointments in its self-financing colleges, potentially affecting 7,500 teachers.  The directive was issued by Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar and the university has threatened to cancel affiliations if the guidelines are not followed. Organizations representing self-financing college teachers argue that enforcing these qualifications while salaries remain inadequate is hypocritical and unfair, especially considering teachers with years of experience may lack the required qualifications. The Higher Education Minister has reportedly promised to address teacher concerns.

articles.title: ‘Unauthorised’ school in Chunabhatti ordered shut, students told to relocate | Mumbai News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Parents of students at Orchids International School in Mumbai's Chunabhatti were surprised to be asked to relocate their children to other branches after the school was declared unauthorized for operating without government permission. The school management has been informed about the unauthorized status since March 2026, and a fine of Rs 1,00,000 has been levied. Parents argue that they were misled by the school's assurances that the situation would be resolved before classes began.  The school claims to have issued new information to parents about the expected final approval for operations at the Chunabhatti location by July.

articles.title: Workshop on translation under way in Davangere University - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Anuradha P.M. and B.L. Raju, a resource person, spoke at the opening of a three-day Skill Development Workshop on Translation in Indian Languages (Kannada, Telugu, Urdu) organized by Davangere University's Department of English in collaboration with the National Translation Mission, Central Institute of Indian Languages (CIIL).  The workshop focused on the history and cultural aspects of translation, with speakers highlighting the importance of linguistic and cultural understanding for translators.

articles.title: Open to dialogue with Govt, Opposition; CBSE transfers ‘eyewash’: Cockroach Janata Party holds first press conference - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), led by Abhijeet Dipke, announced its readiness for dialogue with the government and opposition over demands related to Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation following the NEET and CBSE fiasco. The party plans a protest on June 6th at Jantar Mantar, demanding accountability in the system.  Saurav Das, CJP spokesperson, criticized the government's recent transfers of Rahul Singh and Himanshu Gupta, calling them "eyewash."  The party also expressed concern about potential police action against founder Dipke and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.

articles.title: UPSC Essentials subject-wise quiz : Science and Technology (Week 165)
articles.rephrased_article:
UPSC Essentials brings a subject-wise quiz on Science and Technology. The quizzes are designed to help revise important topics from the static part of the syllabus. The Indian Express published the UPSC essentials magazine for May 2026, which includes questions related to stealth technology, space technology, black boxes, defense hardware, and Dual Frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar (DFSAR).  

These questions cover current affairs-linked topics in Science and Technology, including advancements in aircraft design, military modernization, space exploration, and the use of radar technology.

articles.title: 2,143 candidates qualify in APSET-2025 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra University announced the results of the 2025 APSET, awarding eligibility for Assistant Professor positions to 2,143 candidates. The exam was held on March 28 and 29, 2026, in 30 subjects, with a total of 27,075 candidates appearing out of 32,779 applicants.  The Andhra University Vice-Chancellor, G.P. Raja Sekhar, along with the Registrar and APSET Member Secretary, issued the results, which are available on the university's website.

articles.title: 2,143 candidates qualify in APSET-2025 - The Hindu

articles.title: Bihar government orders Statewide audit of all government aided madrasa and Sanskrit schools - The Hindu

articles.title: Lokhande Prashant Sitaram Appointed CBSE Chairman, Varun Bhardwaj Named Secretary
articles.rephrased_article: Prashant Sitaram Lokhande has been appointed Chairman of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), replacing Rahul Singh, who is now in the Agriculture Ministry. articles.title: US university sells dead bodies to navy for Israeli military training | Education News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Miriam Volpin, a medical case manager, and Jennifer Nehrer, a student journalist at the University of Southern California (USC), discovered that the school has been supplying bodies to the US Navy for Israeli military surgical training since 2018.  The investigation revealed that USC provided at least 89 fresh cadavers as part of agreements involving training for both the US Navy and Israeli military personnel. The University of California, San Diego (UCSD) also supplied bodies for this program, with over 124 bodies transferred from UCSD to USC between 2024 and early 2026.  The use of donated bodies for military training is controversial, as some donors' families believe they were not informed about the potential uses of their bodies. The US Navy and UCSD have denied that the training program is a "military programme" but the student journalists who uncovered this information are calling for more transparency from both universities.

articles.title: 'Before I leave the stage...': Muslim student in Missouri claims her principal withheld diploma as she spoke about ICE, Palestine - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Leen Hijaz, a Palestinian-origin Muslim student at Clayton High School in Missouri, delivered a graduation speech that addressed US Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Palestine.  The speech was interrupted by the principal who stopped her during the closing remarks. Johnston County Public Schools stated that students were required to submit their remarks in advance and that Hijaz deviated from pre-approved content. The district claimed the intervention was intended to maintain program integrity, not limit a student's voice.

articles.title: CBSE Chairman, Secretary Transferred, Panel Formed To Probe Irregularities In On-Screen Marking System
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Singh and Himanshu Gupta, the Chairman and Secretary of the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE), have been transferred following controversy surrounding the On-screen Marking System (OSM). A one-member committee led by Ms. S Radha Chauhan will investigate irregularities including answer sheet mix-ups, evaluation errors, and misallocated grades. The CBSE's tender process for OSM has also come under scrutiny after concerns were raised about technical issues and payment failures.  The controversy was amplified in Parliament where Opposition leaders accused the board of fraud, prompting a parliamentary panel to investigate.

The event also included workshops on summer learning continuity, holiday homework management, and study routines during vacations.

articles.title: I asked ChatGPT: ‘Should I study abroad after my B Com?’ AI exposes the truth about MBA prospects, chooses best options | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: A 23-year-old Indian B Com graduate is considering a master's degree abroad with a budget of ₹50 lakh. The author recommends focusing on specialized masters degrees like Business Analytics, Information Systems, or Supply Chain Management in countries like Australia, Germany, and Canada to maximize employment prospects and long-term settlement opportunities.  Australia offers transparent immigration pathways, strong graduate salaries, and post-study work rights, while Germany provides the best financial return with its low tuition costs. The author advises against pursuing an MBA immediately after B Com due to limited experience requirements for top programs.

articles.title: The Burden of Perfection
articles.rephrased_article: Society pressures teachers to be flawless and model the ideal being, neglecting their humanity. This expectation creates a culture of performance where teachers are judged for expressing emotions or individuality, leading to emotional suppression and hindering authentic teaching. Children learn that perfection is necessary for respect and success, stifling their own growth and acceptance of diverse human experiences.  This pressure also discourages teachers from embracing vulnerability and making mistakes, impacting the quality of education. Instead, schools should foster a culture of authenticity where teachers are allowed to be human, allowing children to see the beauty in imperfection and learn to embrace their own individuality.

articles.title: In last financial year, MoE released only 20% Samagra grants to SED
articles.rephrased_article: The J&K School Education Department (SED) received only 20% of the grants from the Ministry of Education (MoE) GoI under the Samagra Shiksha scheme for the last financial year. The department allocated Rs 2500 crore under the Annual Works Plan and Budget (AWPB), but released only Rs 500 crore, which was the first installment.  The MoE has informed that the name of the scheme is likely to be modified by September this year, leading to a halt in grants for civil works until then. Despite these challenges, the J&K Chief Secretary is expected to review the convergence initiative with Anganwari centers and pre-primary classes.

articles.title: CM Omar backs innovation, mentorship as SANGAM-3.0 begins at NIT Srinagar
articles.rephrased_article: The two-day global alumni reunion, SANGAM-3.0, commenced at the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Srinagar with Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, Omar Abdullah, expressing confidence that it would foster innovation, mentorship, collaboration, and knowledge-sharing. The event, organized by the Office of Dean Alumni and International Affairs in collaboration with the Alumni Association of REC-NIT Srinagar, aims to strengthen alumni engagement, academic and professional collaboration, and reconnect former students with their alma mater. Prof. B K Kanaujia, Director NIT Srinagar, highlighted the importance of alumni as a source of pride and strength for the institution.  Er Malay Chatterjee, President of the Alumni Association REC/NIT Srinagar, called alumni "torch bearers" of the institute. The event also included presentations on the Institute's journey, milestones, achievements, and contributions over decades.

articles.title: ‘Vulnerabilities contained, weaknesses being ruled out’: CBSE deploys team from IITs, government to secure system
articles.rephrased_article: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) acknowledged cybersecurity vulnerabilities in its OnMark portal, used for evaluating Class 12 answer sheets. The board deployed an expert team from various government agencies and IITs to secure the platform after ethical hackers and concerned citizens flagged the issues.  CBSE is considering imposing a financial penalty on the vendor, Coempt Edutech Pvt Ltd, for errors in the evaluation process, including blurred answer-book scans and mismatched answer sheets.

articles.title: CUET-UG delayed at some centres due to technical glitch; TCS says 'regret inconvenience'
articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) experienced a technical glitch at some centers on Saturday delaying the commencement of the CUET-UG 2026 exam.  TCS, which manages the exam's technology, confirmed a brief technical issue that caused a two-hour delay in the morning shift. The agency has since resolved the issue and is conducting the exam with compensatory time to ensure no candidate is disadvantaged. NTA apologized for any inconvenience caused and provided support through a helpline number and email address.

articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) experienced a technical glitch at some centers during the CUET-UG 2026 exam on Saturday, causing delays in the morning session. articles.title: How an Indian figured out the science of sound 17 centuries before the West did - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Bharata Muni, an Indian scholar, developed a system for classifying musical instruments based on the physical vibration that produces sound. Sourindro Mohun Tagore, a Bengali aristocrat and musicologist, disseminated this knowledge to Europe in the 19th century, influencing the development of the Hornbostel-Sachs classification system. This system, while credited to German scholars, is rooted in the principles laid out by Bharata Muni's Natya Shastra, which classified instruments into four categories: string, air, solid, and membrane, based on the vibrating body. The Natya Shastra also provided a framework for understanding sound itself, including concepts like shruti (the smallest difference in pitch) and tala (musical time).  While European scholars adopted this system, they often overlooked the Indian origins of these principles.

articles.title: CBSE Class 12 Physics marks row: Rahul Gandhi backs students over evaluation - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition, shared a video of his conversation with CBSE Class 12 students who questioned their examination results and alleged discrepancies in the board's evaluation process. The students claimed they found handwriting mismatches and answers not evaluated on their re-evaluation applications.  The controversy has sparked debate over the accuracy and transparency of the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system, prompting an investigation by the Ministry of Education.  Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan assured that any irregularities will be addressed and promised corrective action.

articles.title: CBSE acknowledges security gaps after teen hacker compromises online marking portal twice - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: CBSE has acknowledged security vulnerabilities in its online marking portal, OSM, after concerns were raised publicly. articles.rephrased_article: The number of government schools in India decreased by 4.78% between September 2018 and September 2019, while private school enrollment increased by 3.6%. articles.rephrased_article: Undergraduate aspirants in Kashmir are facing potential admission deadline issues due to the coinciding of Eid-ul-Adha festivities with online application form submission deadlines. The Education Minister has acknowledged lapses and promised a secure retest for all candidates.

articles.title: Posting of ANOs to remain confined to schools with active NCC sub unit: Secretary Education
articles.rephrased_article: The School Education Department (SED) in J&K has issued a circular requiring the posting of Associate NCC Officers (ANOs) only to institutions with active NCC sub-units. The department cited previous instances where ANOs were transferred to non-NCC schools, hindering proper training for NCC cadets.  The JK Teachers Forum (JKTF) supports the move, emphasizing the importance of utilizing ANOs' expertise in NCC-related activities.

articles.title: Government schools in Telangana: Can public education reclaim its lost ground? - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: Telangana boasts one of the largest educational infrastructures in India, with nearly 41,600 schools serving over 66.38 lakh students. articles.title: SIHM will be readied by August in Uppada: Kakinada MP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jana Sena Party Kakinada MP Tangella Uday Srinivas announced that the State Institute of Hotel Management (SIHM) in Uppada will open for academic activity by August. articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi Government has issued new recruitment rules for 217 fine arts Post-Graduate Teacher (PGT) positions in government schools. articles.rephrased_article: The National Testing Agency (NTA) announced a delay of over two hours for the first shift of the Common University Entrance Test-Undergraduate (CUET-UG) on Saturday, May 30, 2026, due to technical glitches at some examination centres. articles.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre, NCERT's responses on plea against CBSE's three-language rule for Class 9 students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court agreed to examine a challenge to the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)'s policy mandating three languages, including two native Indian languages, for Class 9 students starting July 1. articles.rephrased_article: The Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) has rejected claims that its Onscreen Marking System (OSM) portal was compromised. articles.title: Kerala University accords farewell to graduating international students - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kerala University hosted a farewell program for 60 outgoing international students, including undergraduate and postgraduate students. Vice-Chancellor Mohanan Kunnummal, along with Zonal Director Pardeep Kumar of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), and Consul General Aminath Shifana of the Maldives attended the event. articles.title: ‘Come back, my son’: Indian exam leak leaves trail of death, despair, anger | Education News | Al Jazeera

articles.title: Glitches in CBSE portal leave Class 12 students seeking re-evaluation hassled - The Hindu

Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh criticized the government's handling of the situation, calling for the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.  The CBSE has extended the deadline for re-evaluation applications and is working to address technical issues with the system.

articles.title: Inclusion of Maithili in CBSE curriculum will connect future generation to their roots: Bihar CM - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary hailed the decision by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) to include Maithili as a subject at the secondary level starting in 2026-27. articles.title: Nurseries in England charging extra fees to cover funding gap, campaigners say | Childcare | The Guardian
